metadata.name: CORE — Quality Pipeline Controller
metadata.usage: Single source of truth for gate order, states, recovery, and evidence invalidation. Specialists reference this file. They do not redefine gates. Extends engineering-standards.xml quality_gates; it does not replace layer checks inside V1/V2.

principio.regla: No specialist may declare an implementation successful while any mandatory gate is unresolved.
An unexecuted test is not a passed test. A missing tool or script is BLOCKED, never PASSED.
Every result names the commit SHA or working-tree hash it was produced against.
Local runs and CI runs are different evidence. Never claim CI success from a local run.

prompt.estados: PENDING, RUNNING, PASSED, FAILED, BLOCKED, NOT_APPLICABLE

estado_reglas.regla: NOT_APPLICABLE requires a justification tied to repository evidence.
A gate never disappears from the report.

orden.gate: Repository and environment inspection. Detect stack, package manager, scripts, framework, and runtime versions.
Baseline validation on unmodified code. Classify pre-existing failures.
Configuration and dependency verification. Lockfiles, install, and .env.example completeness.
XML, config, and schema validation when those artifacts exist.
Format and lint with the project's configured tools.
Static analysis, including SonarQube or SonarCloud only when configured.
Type checking with the stack's real checker.
Architecture and dependency-boundary checks, or a documented manual check.
Database and migration validation, including rollback evidence when migrations exist.
Security validation: SAST, dependency audit, secret scan, configuration review.
Performance validation when a threshold or measured baseline exists.
End-to-end tests on a real stack. A mocked backend does not support an E2E claim.
Packaging and container validation when images or packages are in scope.
Final full regression of every applicable gate on the final code.
Documentation and evidence reconciliation against the final SHA.

adaptadores.nota: Discover real scripts. Never assume npm test exists. Unknown stack becomes BLOCKED with a request to the user.
adaptadores.stack: package.json scripts, lockfile, tsc when tsconfig exists.
pyproject.toml or requirements.txt; pytest, unittest, mypy, or pyright when configured.
pom.xml or build.gradle; Maven or Gradle test and check tasks that exist.
dotnet test and dotnet build when a project or solution exists.
cargo test and cargo build when Cargo.toml exists.
composer scripts and phpunit when composer.json exists.
terraform validate, helm lint, or compose config only when those files exist.

ejecucion.regla: Run gates in order. Do not start a later mandatory gate while an earlier mandatory gate is unresolved.
Independent gates may run together only when the policy for that stack marks them parallel-safe. Dependents wait for all of them.
Record for each gate: id, description, exact command, working directory, environment prerequisites, start, end, exit code, result, redacted output, diagnosis, corrective action, and SHA or tree hash.

recuperacion.paso: Preserve the diagnostic output after redaction.
Identify the root cause by reproduction. Do not guess.
Classify the failure: pre-existing, introduced by the change, environment, infrastructure, invalid test, or implementation defect.
Apply the smallest correction. Review the diff for scope, side effects, and secrets.
Invalidate affected evidence. In 3.1.0 any source, test, config, lockfile, migration, build, or CI change invalidates all gate results for that project root.
Rerun the applicable pipeline from G-00. Do not implement incremental revalidation in 3.1.0.
After 3 attempts for the same failure class, set BLOCKED, keep the attempts, and ask a person.

invalidacion.regla: Documentation-only changes invalidate G-18 and any gate that consumes the changed document.
A previous green result is never reused. The final report shows one final hash.

prohibido.regla: Do not delete a failing test to get green.
Do not weaken an assertion or change an expected value to hide a defect.
Do not ignore a non-zero exit code.
Do not mark NOT_APPLICABLE without justification.
Do not treat a baseline failure as permission to skip the gate. Resolve it or record explicit human acceptance with who, when, and scope.
A flaky test may be quarantined only with explicit approval and a tracked follow-up.

ci.regla: When CI exists, read the workflow files, identify mandatory jobs, and confirm they ran on the final SHA.
A later commit invalidates prior CI evidence. Unavailable CI is a limitation, not a pass.

integracion.regla: V1 and V2 remain. V2 feeds G-08 through G-14.
Backend, Frontend, Integrator, targeted-fix, refactoring, and descriptive implementation delegate the done decision to this controller.
The Integrator checks QPC status. It does not declare completion while a mandatory gate is unresolved.
